FUTURE OPTION — multi-slice rest-capture via greedy backtracking
================================================================

Status:   NOT IMPLEMENTED. Deliberately deferred during the §11.1
          trailing-rest-capture work (branch runtime/machine-loop-
          actions). Recorded here so the idea doesn't have to be
          rediscovered; take it up only if a real program needs it.

Context:  §11.1 was provisionally resolved as trailing-only, var-only
          rest capture: one `var!` per tuple pattern, final position,
          zero-or-more elements. Mid capture was rejected because,
          under the natural "find an assignment" reading, a pattern
          like (a, b!, c, d!) leaves the alignment of the fixed
          elements (where does `c` sit?) indeterminate, and mid and
          trailing capture were resolved to be mutually exclusive
          without language extensions.

The deferred option (as sketched in session discussion):

  Allow MULTIPLE rest captures per pattern (mid and trailing alike)
  with a deterministic slicing strategy:

    - Each capture is GREEDY, taken LEFT TO RIGHT.
    - After each greedy slice, BACKTRACK the last capture's width
      until every non-`!` (fixed) element of the pattern finds a
      binding.

  e.g.  ("log", msg!, level)   vs   ("log", "x", "y", 3)
        msg! greedily takes ("x", "y", 3), backtracks until `level`
        binds → msg! = ("x", "y"), level = 3.

Why it was not implemented:

  - Nothing in the current design needs it. Trailing-only covers the
    known consumers: the §6.4 default Error machine `(c!) : panic c`,
    and cons-tail capture for the §9 list sugar (`(Cons, H, T!)`).
  - Backtracking-in-the-matcher is a real semantics change: §3.2
    says matching is commitment — match success and commitment are
    the same event. A backtracking matcher would need a guarded
    trial phase for the slice search before commitment, which cuts
    against the "no guard/rollback concept" resolution unless very
    carefully framed (the search is internal to one structural
    match, but it still means a pattern can fail *after* partially
    binding — observable only via error messages, since nothing
    outside the match sees intermediate envs).
  - It is, verbatim, "a funny option with good footguns": greedy
    left-to-right with backtracking is deterministic but deeply
    surprising to reason about (the binding of an earlier capture
    depends on later fixed elements). That is arguably ON BRAND for
    a language about races — which is exactly why it is written down
    here instead of being dismissed.

If picked up later:

  - Parser: drop the trailingOnly check in tuplePat (Parser.hs),
    keep var-only.
  - Matcher: replace matchTuple's single-PRest case with the greedy
    backtrack search over capture widths (Runtime.hs). Requires the
    §3.2 framing decision above to be made explicitly in the
    handover first.
  - Handover: §11.1 and §12 ("matcher checks structure") both need
    amending; add tests for capture-dependent alignment, including
    the case where two different alignments of the same fixed
    elements are possible and greedy-left must pick the earliest
    split that lets all fixed elements bind.

Full context: lindana-handover.md §11.1 and the trailing-capture
decision note in §13.

**The note** (`agent-history/messageboard/multi-slice-rest-capture-future.txt`, house style matching the §11.2 note): greedy left-to-right slices, backtrack until all non-`!` elements bind — recorded as deliberately deferred, with the two reasons written down so whoever picks it up can't skip them: nothing needs it today, and backtracking-in-the-matcher has a §3.2 tension (matching-is-commitment would need a framed-out internal trial phase) plus the "deterministic but deeply surprising" property — which is exactly why it's a *funny* option worth keeping, and exactly why it's not built now.

**The §11.1 implementation** (`edcfbdc`, 53 tests green ×3, clean on `-Wall`):

- **Syntax**: `PRest Name`, renders as `x!` (round-trips).
- **Parser**: trailing-only and var-only enforced — mid capture (`(a, b!, c)`) and non-var capture (`(Foo!)`) are parse errors, with the mutual-exclusivity rationale documented at the definition site.
- **Matcher**: `matchTuple` — trailing `PRest` binds a sub-tuple of the remaining elements, zero-or-more, so `(c!)` matches any tuple (and doesn't match non-tuples — structural, per §3.2). One subtlety surfaced by testing: captures route through the `PVar` bind-or-check path, so `(n, n!)` honors the §11.2 equality rule rather than overwriting.
- **Tests**: 6 matcher-level, 3 parser accept/reject/round-trip, and 1 end-to-end — `(Ping, rest!) : out (Pong, rest!)` rebuilding the tuple through the full machine loop, which is the capture↔splice inversion the continuation-passing design leans on.

---
name: session-dump
description: Dump the current pi session into the project's agent-history/harness-sessions/ directory as a pair of files — a raw JSONL (machine-readable) and a conversation markdown (human-readable), both named <session-name>-<timestamp>. Use whenever the user asks to dump, save, export, or hand off the session history to agent-history/, or at the end of a work session when asked to record a handover.
---

# Session dump

Write the current conversation to `agent-history/harness-sessions/` so the human can review or hand it off later. Do **not** read the dump files back into context — the script prints a one-line summary; that's all you need.

## Usage

```bash
node .pi/skills/session-dump/scripts/dump-session.mjs            # auto name (from /name, else "session")
node .pi/skills/session-dump/scripts/dump-session.mjs "fix tuple-space races"   # explicit name
node .pi/skills/session-dump/scripts/dump-session.mjs --quiet    # just print the two paths
```

Optional flags: `--name <name>` (session name), `--out <dir>` (default: `<cwd>/agent-history/harness-sessions`).

## What it produces (matches the project's existing dump convention)

- `agent-history/harness-sessions/machine-readable/<original-session-filename>.jsonl` — verbatim copy of the live session JSONL (full fidelity: tool calls, results, branches).
- `agent-history/harness-sessions/human-readable/<session-name>--pi-session-<original-stem>.md` — readable transcript: user + assistant text, tool calls as one-liners, tool results omitted.

If the session has no `/name`, pass one explicitly — the name is what makes the human-readable dump findable.

The script finds the current session automatically (`PI_SESSION_FILE` when run inside pi, newest-session fallback otherwise). Run it from the project root so the default output paths resolve.

## When to use it

- The user asks to "dump the session", "save this to agent-history", or similar.
- The user asks for a handover document — dump first, then (only if asked) write a curated handover doc separately; the dump is the raw record, not the handover.
- If the session has no name yet and the user wants a specific one, pass it as an argument rather than telling the user to run `/name`.
